note: The Notification hook on the wire, which docs/captures/claude/ held none of: hooks-2.1.222 recorded 38 invocations and zero Notification events, because a headless run auto-denies and never raises a prompt. Interactive sessions driven through tmux, one arm per session. Shapes and one enum value only.

registration: the capture hook passed additively through `claude --settings <file>`, so no settings file was edited and the real ~/.claude/settings.json was never written
note: NOT an isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. That route was attempted first and hit the wall this directory's README already records: it changes the credential's keychain account name and loses the subscription login, so the session demands an OAuth code. `--settings` is additive and keeps the real credential.

capture_hook.py now records this ONE payload value, and only on Notification. It is a closed vocabulary the harness picks from rather than text anyone wrote, so it is the same class of fact as `tool`: a name, not an argument. Without it a capture can prove a Notification arrived and nothing about whether the adapter classifies it correctly, which was the whole question. `message` is still not recorded: it is prose, and on a permission prompt it names the command being approved. One ambiguity to know when reading these: a `notification_type` that arrives as a non-string is recorded as an empty string, so "" on a Notification line means either absent or not-a-string. It has never been observed as either; every record here carries a real value.

claim: which notification_type a plain main-session permission prompt carries
was: INFERRED - read from the emit sites of an installed 2.1.226 bundle, and recorded as an open question in docs/design-needs-input.md
verdict: CONFIRMED. It is the value ACTIONABLE_NOTIFICATION_TYPES already contains, so the shipped classification is correct and nothing needed changing. Raised twice from different tools (a NotebookEdit file edit and an MCP tool-use approval), same value both times.

now: MEASURED: `elicitation_dialog`, from a real MCP elicitation dialog open in the client
how: Nothing Cargento ships can raise one - ask_operator is a blocking tool call, a different protocol feature - so the probe used a throwaway stdlib MCP server that answers tools/call and then sends `elicitation/create` at the client. No Node runtime, on the precedent the ask-lane hold probe set.
verdict: CONFIRMED, and it is in ACTIONABLE_NOTIFICATION_TYPES.

now: MEASURED: `idle_prompt`, captured incidentally when a session went quiet mid-run
verdict: CONFIRMED as the current spelling. The `idle_timeout` alias in IDLE_NOTIFICATION_TYPES was not observed and remains a compatibility guess.

claim: a worker's network request has no PermissionRequest behind it
now: STILL INFERRED. Not settled by this run.
detail: `worker_permission_prompt` was never produced. A subagent asked to use a tool outside the allow list surfaced a plain `permission_prompt` on the same session prefix as the leader, alongside a `PermissionRequest` carrying tool=NotebookEdit. So the TOOL half demonstrably has both signals, which is consistent with the claim's reasoning without proving its network half. Settling it needs a worker network request that is not allow-listed, which this arrangement could not produce.

note: The trap that voids this measurement, and it is subtler than the headless one. A session that loads the operator's own user settings can be unable to raise a prompt at all: the settings here carry defaultMode `bypassPermissions` AND a bare allow list of Bash, Read, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep, WebSearch and WebFetch. `--permission-mode default` overrides the MODE and not the ALLOW LIST, so every common tool still runs unapproved and the first run recorded nothing while looking like it worked. The fix is to drive a tool outside that list; NotebookEdit was the one used here.

question: Does the Notification path carry what notifications.py assumes?
answer: Yes for three of the four values it branches on, and the fourth is untested rather than wrong.
detail: permission_prompt, elicitation_dialog and idle_prompt measured, all classified as the code already assumed. worker_permission_prompt not produced. prompt_id is on the payload, and on most Claude hook events in hooks-2.1.222 -- not all: SessionStart carries none, which fits a per-turn identity minted when a turn begins. So it identifies the turn rather than the notification and cannot key a per-nudge alert. Whether it is constant within a turn is not settled by key names alone.
